etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English gunne, gonne, possibly from Gunnhild, a female given name formerly used as a nickname for engines of war. The name is composed of the Norse elements gunnr and hildr, both meaning "battle".

definitions.definition: A very portable, short firearm, for hand use, which fires bullets or projectiles, such as a handgun, revolver, pistol, or Derringer.
A less portable, long firearm that fires bullets or projectiles; a rifle, either manual, automatic or semi-automatic; a flintlock, musket or shotgun.
(military) A cannon with relatively long barrel, operating with relatively low angle of fire, and having a high muzzle velocity.[1]
(military) A cannon with a 6-inch/155mm minimum nominal bore diameter and tube length 30 calibers or more. See also: howitzer; mortar.[1]
(figurative) A firearm or cannon used for saluting or signalling.21-gun salute

quote.citation: 1906, Stanley J[ohn] Weyman, chapter I, in Chippinge Borough, New York, N.Y.: McClure, Phillips & Co., →OCLC, page 01:
quote.text: It was April 22, 1831, and a young man was walking down Whitehall in the direction of Parliament Street. […]. He halted opposite the Privy Gardens, and, with his face turned skywards, listened until the sound of the Tower guns smote again on the ear and dispelled his doubts.

definitions.definition: A device for projecting a hard object very forcefully; a firearm or cannon.

quote.citation: 1879, R[ichard] J[efferies], chapter 1, in The Amateur Poacher, London: Smith, Elder, & Co., […], →OCLC:
quote.text: They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. Otherwise his pelt would not have been so perfect.

definitions.definition: Any implement designed to fire a projectile from a tube.
A device or tool that projects a substance.
A device or tool that applies something rather than projecting it.
A device operated by a trigger and acting in a manner similar to a firearm.
(surfing) A long surfboard designed for surfing big waves (not the same as a longboard, a gun has a pointed nose and is generally a little narrower).

quote.text: by the winter of 1962, the Brewer Surfboards Hawaii gun was the most in-demand big-wave equipment on the North Shore.

definitions.definition: (cellular automata) A pattern that "fires" out other patterns.

definitions.definition: (colloquial, usually in the plural) The biceps.
(nautical, in the plural) Violent blasts of wind.
(Australia, slang) Someone excellent, surpassingly wonderful, or cool.
(transitive) To cause to speed up.
(informal) To offer vigorous support to (a person or cause).
(informal) (gunning for something or gunning to do something) make a great effort.
